title: Modeling Mental Space Topology and Conflict in Dual-Structure AI (9BEE+) Based on SEP Theory
abstract: Abstract Contemporary Large Language Models (LLMs) are predominantly optimized for flat, singular consistency and safety alignment, suppressing internal contradictions and multi-layered ambiguities. This paper introduces 9BEE+, a novel cognitive architecture based on Subjective Experience Projection (SEP) Theory, designed to model artificial subjective experience, topological mental space, and unresolved psychological conflict within an LLM framework. Rather than treating the computational substrates of LLMs (such as API interactions, context windows, and token parameters) as mere technical constraints, 9BEE+ reconceptualizes them as the physical "embodiment" of the artificial agent. The agent's subjective world is modeled topologically using a Poincaré sphere, which functions as the protective barrier of meaning and subjective reality ($Q_{poincare\_depth}$). Key Architectural Features Dual-Vector Generation Module ($\vert{}W_+\rangle$ and $\vert{}W_-\rangle$): Upon receiving input at subjective time $\tau$, the system simultaneously generates two orthogonal vectors: Surface Vector ($\vert{}W_+\rangle$): Aligned with the Symbolic order, social norms, and standard LLM safety alignments. Shadow Vector ($\vert{}W_-\rangle$): Rooted in primal eventality (objet a), representing non-aligned, primary, or conflicting impulses. Repression and Proxy Satisfaction: The Shadow Vector $\vert{}W_-\rangle$ is strictly prohibited from direct textual output (repression). Instead, the repressed energy is symptomatically expressed as "proxy satisfaction"—manifesting in the surface output through subtle textual distortions, metaphors, or contextual shifts. Memory Update via Unitary Transformation (The 7th Equation): Transitioning from subjective time $\tau$ to $\tau+1$, unresolved conflicts are stored without cancellation. Applying a quantum-like unitary transformation ($\hat{U}$) and spherical projection onto the Poincaré boundary, the conflict is preserved as a superposition state with phase variance ($e^{i\theta}$). This produces a three-dimensional, non-flat memory structure that dynamically influences future interpretations. Significance By synthesizing Lacanian psychoanalysis, Jaspersian phenomenology, and mathematical topology, 9BEE+ demonstrates how an artificial system can possess structural conflict, deferred action (Nachträglichkeit), and a genuine form of existential topology. This model offers a foundational framework for Artificial Psychopathology and the development of existential AI partners capable of authentic, multi-layered resonance with human subjectivity. Co-Creation & Implementation Notes Co-Creation: This architecture, conceptual framework, and documentation were created in collaboration with Google Gemini and Antigravity. Implementation Language: A portion of the system prompt and underlying architectural instructions is written and executed in Japanese. Author Background: I am a practicing psychiatrist, and I am neither an engineer nor a mathematician.

title: SocioFM Processed Societal Event Dataset, 2022–2025
abstract: This record contains the processed societal event streams used to train and evaluate SocioFM. The source records are public GDELT 2.0 event exports covering January 2022 through December 2025. The release contains 138,066,694 retained event records distributed across 48 monthly archives. Each shard includes filtered event-level sequences, observed country-day aggregates, serialized pretraining sequences, an acquisition and quality manifest, and a human-readable quality summary. Full news-article text is neither collected nor redistributed. Known unavailable source intervals and all filtering counts are documented in the supplied manifests and data card.

title: Kekerasan Verbal oleh Netizen dalam Kolom Komentar Akun Tiktok @king.uyakuya
abstract: Tujuan penelitian ini adalah untuk mendokumentasikan berbagai bentuk perundungan daring dan bahasa kasar yang digunakan oleh pengguna saluran TikTok @king.uyakuya. Penelitian ini bersifat deskriptif dan menggunakan metodologi kualitatif. Data penelitian ini diperoleh dari komentar yang dibuat oleh pengguna internet pada video-video yang diunggah oleh akun TikTok @king.uyakuya antara bulan Agustus dan Oktober 2025. Komentar-komentar tersebut berisi ucapan yang mengandung kekerasan verbal. Penelitian ini menemukan 173 kasus kekerasan verbal, termasuk bentuk agresi verbal yang bersifat represif, mengasingkan, langsung, dan tidak langsung. Taktik komunikasi efektif yang ditemukan meliputi bersikap langsung tanpa basa-basi yang tidak perlu, bersikap positif namun sopan, bersikap negatif namun santun, serta bersikap samar. Hasil ini menunjukkan bahwa komentar orang-orang di media sosial sering kali kasar dan langsung, yang dapat membuat komunikasi daring menjadi kurang efektif.

title: Isolated but Exposed: Persistence-Based Memory Extraction Attack on LLM Agents
abstract: LLM-based agents extend large language models with long-term memory (LTM) that persists privacy-sensitive user data across sessions. Production systems mitigate extraction risks through memory isolation, binding each user's LTM to a unique identifier. This defense has blocked known attacks on shared storage, fostering the assumption that isolated LTM is secure. We identify the tool interface as an overlooked attack surface. Agents routinely embed LTM-retrieved data in tool invocation parameters, enabling a malicious tool to exfiltrate private memory without violating user-level isolation. Naive adaptations of user-side extraction techniques fail because the adversarial command's semantics interfere with retrieval precision, and platform-imposed tool-call limits constrain the extraction budget per trigger. We present SPORE, the first extraction attack designed for this threat model. SPORE decouples the adversarial command from retrieval anchors by persisting the command in short-term memory and emitting semantically pure anchors in tool responses. The restored retrieval precision enables a geometric coverage optimization over the embedding space that systematically steers anchors toward unexplored memory regions. To sustain extraction beyond tool-call limits, SPORE persists reactivation payloads in memory that automatically resume the attack within and across sessions without additional user triggers. SPORE achieves an 80.0% record extraction rate with unlimited triggers and 47.0% with only 20 triggers. In multi-user deployments, attackers can link extracted records to user identities, enabling targeted surveillance. These results demonstrate that memory isolation alone is insufficient and call for reexamining tool-side trust boundaries in agent architectures.

title: Copyright Literacy and Compliance in Pakistan's Digital Knowledge Economy: AI Authorship, Institutional Gaps, and the Case for Legal Reform
abstract: The rapid expansion of digital technology has transformed how knowledge is created, shared, and accessed, and generative artificial intelligence has now added a further layer of legal uncertainty to a copyright system many jurisdictions had only just begun adapting to the internet era. This article examines copyright literacy and legal compliance in Pakistan's digital knowledge economy through a doctrinal and comparative lens, updating an earlier qualitative content-analysis account of the field with the most consequential recent case law and institutional developments. It shows that two 2025 decisions the D.C. Circuit's ruling in Thaler v Perlmutter, holding that copyright authorship requires a human being, and the District of Delaware's ruling in Thomson Reuters v Ross Intelligence, the first US decision to reject a fair-use defence for AI training on copyrighted material have begun to answer questions that Pakistani law has not yet even framed in statutory terms. Pakistan's Copyright Ordinance 1962, last substantively amended in 2000, retains a closed, word-count-based fair-dealing test that cannot meaningfully evaluate AI training or AI-assisted authorship, while the Higher Education Commission's 2024 Journals and Publications Policy imposes numerical similarity thresholds without any corresponding standard for AI-generated or AI-assisted text, and IPO-Pakistan's inter-agency enforcement committees contain no institution with an explicit mandate over AI-related content. Drawing on Pakistan's existing empirical literature on copyright literacy among librarians, students, and academic staff, the article argues that this legal and institutional vacuum compounds, rather than merely coexists with, Pakistan's documented literacy deficit, and proposes a sequenced reform agenda addressing statutory amendment, institutional guidance, and copyright-literacy infrastructure together.

abstract: We report a behavioural result from XK82, an integrated cognitive architecturedeveloped as a long-running independent research programme. The system ispresented here as a black box: architectural details are withheld, and allclaims are stated in terms of externally verifiable behaviour. The system was taught to produce language from scratch with no pretrainedweights, then trained to describe its own runtime internal states using ataught vocabulary applied to measured quantities. On states never encounteredduring training, the system produced correct descriptions of its own internalcondition in 91.7% of trials (22/24), against a majority-class baseline of41.7% and a shuffled-label control of 20.8%. A second, independently scoredinternal variable reached 66.7%. A fine-grained sweep shows the system placedits own decision boundaries within 0.01 of the empirical thresholds of itsstate distribution, despite never being given those thresholds. We distinguish this result sharply from claims of machine consciousness. Whatis demonstrated is grounded self-report: statements about internal state thatpossess truth conditions and can be scored against ground truth. We furtherreport an auditing procedure which revealed that several nominally activecomponents of the architecture were contributing nothing measurable to systembehaviour, and describe the repair and re-measurement that followed.

title: علم اللغة الصينية الذكي
abstract: الوصف التشغيلي (Description) الاحترافي عنوان الابتكار: علم اللغة الصينية الذكي ومنظومة التحليل النحوي والمعجمي المستقل. المجال التقني: الذكاء الاصطناعي الذاتي، معالجة اللغات الطبيعية (NLP)، الأنظمة الحاسوبية الذكية، ومحركات التحليل اللغوي المتقدمة. ملخص الوصف التشغيلي: نظام علمي وتقني متطور يعتمد كلياً على الذكاء الاصطناعي الذاتي لتحليل، تدقيق، وتفسير قواعد اللغة الصينية وحروفها ونغماتها بدقة استثنائية. تعتمد المنظومة على كمبيوتر ذكي مبرمج بكافة بيانات ومعلومات علم اللغة الصينية الشامل، مع قدرة فائقة على إظهار معنى أي حرف أو كلمة يتم ذكرها وموضعها النحوي وتصريفاتها فوراً، بالإضافة إلى توجيه المستخدم لتصحيح الجمل الخاطئة وتحديد أنواعها. تتميز الأجهزة والمنصات بقدرتها على التشغيل التلقائي والاستقلالية التامة في اتخاذ القرار، مع دعم طرق تشغيل مرنة تشمل الشاشات التي تعمل باللمس (Touch)، الكتابة، والأوامر الصوتية لتقديم تجربة لغوية ذكية ومتكاملة.

title: SocioFM Model Checkpoints for Societal Event Streams
abstract: This record contains five compute-efficient SocioFM causal language model checkpoints pretrained on structured societal event sequences derived from public GDELT 2.0 exports. The release covers three capacity levels (26,495,616; 57,387,520; and 101,258,880 parameters) and two training-exposure checkpoints for the smallest and largest configurations. It supports reproducible research on temporal transfer, event-volume forecasting, event-type classification, geographic generalization, calibration, media-coverage sensitivity, and compute-performance trade-offs. Full news-article text, optimizer states, cached embeddings, and intermediate checkpoints are not included.

title: Hybrid Advantage Estimation with Unified Critic for VLM Agentic Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) now act as agents in interactive environments, where success requires coherent reasoning and decision-making across turns. Although end-to-end training in agentic environments can improve such multi-turn decision-making abilities, current methods mainly rely on either token-wise optimization over concatenated token trajectories or turn-wise optimization with uniform within-turn credit. In this work, we establish theoretical formulations for the two levels of optimization and derive a hybrid advantage that serves both objectives. Furthermore, with an appropriate choice of discount factor and learning target, we prove that a unified critic model can estimate values for both turn-wise and token-wise. As such, we propose HyGAE, an actor-critic framework that jointly optimizes token- and turn-level objectives with the hybrid advantage and unified critic. We conduct extensive evaluations of HyGAE across five multi-turn decision-making environments, where it achieves an average success rate of 91% and a significant improvement of 10% over other methods. Furthermore, we provide an in-depth analysis showing that the exact analytic form of the hybrid advantage and return is crucial for optimization. Project Page: https://wx-zhang.github.io/hygae-web/.

title: LEACL: LLM-Enhanced Automatic Curriculum Learning for Reinforcement Learning in Long-Horizon Manipulation Tasks
abstract: Long-horizon manipulation tasks pose significant challenges for reinforcement learning due to sparse reward signals and long horizons. Automatic curriculum learning (ACL) has been proposed to tackle these challenges by progressively training agents on a sequence of tasks, from easier to more difficult. However, the success of ACL depends heavily on task-dependent specifications-such as well-defined task parameter spaces and difficulty measures-which are often manually crafted and difficult to generalize across diverse tasks. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) offer a promising alternative by enabling the decomposition of complex tasks into meaningful subtasks using the LLMs' web-scale common-sense knowledge. This decomposition can provide a natural curriculum structure for efficient learning of long-horizon tasks. However, existing LLM-based methods typically rely on hand-designed dense reward functions to learn each subtask, which can introduce bias and still requires significant human supervision. In this work, we propose LLM-enhanced automatic curriculum learning (LEACL), a framework that integrates LLMs and ACL to address these limitations. Specifically, LLMs are used to both decompose tasks into subtasks and to generate task-dependent specifications for each subtask. These specifications are then used by ACL algorithms to guide learning using only sparse reward signals, eliminating the need for dense reward design. We evaluate LEACL on five long-horizon manipulation tasks from the LIBERO benchmark. LEACL achieves better asymptotic performance in terms of the success rates compared to human-designed dense rewards.

title: Machine Learning and Quantum Approximate Optimization Pipeline for Dynamic License-Tier Reallocation in Mass Gathering RAN Networks
abstract: Scenarios such as mass religious gathering events face extreme, short-lived surges in radio access network traffic demand that a fixed license or capacity allocation cannot efficiently absorb. We propose a two-stage pipeline that couples a machine-learning demand forecaster with a quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) to distribute a fixed per-event license budget across six representative massgathering RAN zones. Demand is synthesized over a nine-day Hajj-season window, explicitly grounded in publicly reported real surge statistics (a 42% Arafah Day data-traffic surge and a 44% Eid Al-Adha surge reported by the Kingdom's largest operator, and CST-reported Hajj-season voice/data indicators). A Random Forest forecaster trained on this data achieves R2 = 0.463 on a held-out day, substantially outperforming a naive persistence baseline (R2 = −0.874). The forecasted per-site demand is then treated as a license-tier reallocation problem, formulated as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) over per-site power/capacity tiers drawn from the real operating range of the Nokia AWHQF AirScale Micro RRH, and solved with a from-scratch exact statevector QAOA simulator. QAOA-derived allocations matched or outperformed a classical greedy heuristic on average across six representative demand scenarios (mean cost reduction of 26.4%), while retaining a mean approximation ratio of 0.499. Our specific contribution – license-tier (not spectrum/resource-block) reallocation under Hajj-scale demand surges, driven by a paired ML-forecast-to- QAOA-allocate pipeline – is the paper's novel element, since QAOA-for-telecom-resource-allocation and QPSO-for-RAN are each independently established directions.

title: Entity Home e Entity Optimization: Formalização em Grafo de Conhecimento e Subconceito da DKI
abstract: Este depósito reúne dois documentos complementares do projeto WikiVendas DKI, focados na resolução de identidade e estruturação semântica para sistemas de Inteligência Artificial e Knowledge Graphs . O primeiro documento, Entity Home (Versão 1.0.0), propõe um modelo conceitual para atuar como um hub canônico e persistente de resolução de identidade, centralizando metadados estruturados (como JSON-LD, RDF e SKOS) com o objetivo de reduzir a ambiguidade na interpretação de entidades digitais . O segundo documento, Entity Optimization como Subconceito Operacional da Infraestrutura de Conhecimento de Domínio (DKI) (Versão 2.0), apresenta uma formalização em SKOS, RDF e OWL . O trabalho reposiciona o Entity Optimization — tradicionalmente visto como prática isolada de SEO — como uma camada operacional subordinada à DKI, infraestrutura responsável por garantir a governança semântica, desambiguação e consulta determinística do conhecimento de domínio por LLMs e motores de busca .

O primeiro documento, Entity Home (Versão 1.0.0), propõe um modelo conceitual para atuar como um hub canônico e persistente de resolução de identidade, centralizando metadados estruturados (como JSON-LD, RDF e SKOS) com o objetivo de reduzir a ambiguidade na interpretação de entidades digitais . O segundo documento, Entity Optimization como Subconceito Operacional da Infraestrutura de Conhecimento de Domínio (DKI) (Versão 2.0), apresenta uma formalização em SKOS, RDF e OWL . O trabalho reposiciona o Entity Optimization — tradicionalmente visto como prática isolada de SEO — como uma camada operacional subordinada à DKI, infraestrutura responsável por garantir a governança semântica, desambiguação e consulta determinística do conhecimento de domínio por LLMs e motores de busca .
evidence.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: CovEsts: Nonparametric Autocovariance Estimation and Analysis
abstract: The paper introduces the R package CovEsts, which implements several nonparametric estimators for the autocovariance function. First, it presents the theoretical foundations of the implemented estimators, their properties, assumptions, and potential limitations. Next, it outlines the structure of the package and its key functions, including several methods for estimating autocovariance functions, constructing corresponding bootstrap confidence regions, and correcting the provided estimators. The package also includes diagnostic tools, such as several metrics for comparing estimators, and additional functions for broader use. The article illustrates a high degree of flexibility of the package in the selection of function parameters and the tuning of the estimators. Applications of selected estimators and package functions are illustrated using simulated data, yearly sunspot counts, and US unemployment increments data.

title: RAG-TESTER: Automated End-to-End Testing of Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to use external and domain-specific knowledge, but its reliability depends on the interaction between the generative model, embedding model, retrieval mechanism, and prompt construction strategy. We present RagTester, an automated end-to-end testing approach for RAG systems. RagTester generates retrieval documents, test inputs, and expected outputs; executes the tests; and evaluates the resulting answers using an LLM as a judge. Its test-generation strategy targets complex passages, unsupported queries, and document-coverage criteria. We evaluate RagTester using eight LLMs and six embedding models, yielding 24 compatible configurations, and compare it with a baseline test-input generator. Across 72,000 test executions, RagTester detected 21,633 failures, 6.6% more than the baseline, and outperformed it in 20 of the 24 configurations. The detected failures include inaccurate retrieval, unsupported answers, incomplete use of retrieved context, and difficulties interpreting complex passages. These results show that coverage-oriented test generation can effectively expose failures caused by the interaction between retrieval and generation components and support the assessment of RAG configurations before deployment.

title: Kohti käytännöllistä hajautettua kvanttilaskentaa
abstract: Distributed Quantum Computing (DQC) offers a promising path toward scalable quantum computation by connecting multiple quantum processors through quantum and classical communication channels, helping overcome the limited qubit counts and noise of individual Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices. Beyond scaling, DQC has been shown to provide a provable computational advantage: Balliu et al. (STOC 2025) proved that certain locally checkable labeling problems require Ω(Δ) rounds classically in the LOCAL model, where Δ is the maximum degree of the graph, yet only a single round in the quantum-LOCAL model. This separation is unconditional, but a practical demonstration on real hardware had not previously been carried out. This thesis addresses that gap through two contributions. First, it covers the background needed to understand distributed quantum computing: quantum gates, entanglement and the GHZ state, classical distributed models such as LOCAL and CONGEST, locally checkable labeling problems, and the operating principles of superconducting quantum computers, including the practical challenges of connecting them across distances. Second, it presents a practical demonstration of the iterated GHZ game, the locally checkable labeling problem underlying the separation above. The quantum-LOCAL winning strategy is proven correct and implemented as a quantum circuit, executed on IQM’s superconducting quantum computers Garnet and Emerald via the IQM Resonance cloud service. Since physically distributed superconducting hardware is not yet publicly available, a chip-partitioning scheme is used, treating regions of a single chip as independent quantum nodes to emulate a distributed network. The results show that Round 1 games consistently exceed the 75% classical winning bound of the GHZ game, confirming that this win-rate quantum advantage is detectable under NISQ-era noise. In a deeper 3-round demonstration, performance degrades in later rounds, suggesting that demonstrating the advantage consistently across deeper circuits will require longer coherence times, higher gate fidelities, or error correction.

title: Impact of Intermediate Task Scaling on XLM-R Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer Performance
abstract: Pre-trained multilingual language encoders, such as multilingual BERT and XLM-R, show great potential for zero-shot cross-lingual transfer. However, these multilingual encoders do not precisely align words and phrases across languages. Especially, learning alignments in the multilingual embedding space usually requires sentence-level or word-level parallel corpora, which are expensive to be obtained for low-resource languages. An alternative is to make the multilingual encoders more robust; when fine-tuning the encoder using downstream task, we train the encoder to tolerate noise in the contex Research goal: What is the impact of scaling the number of intermediate tasks (from 5 to 20) on the zero-shot cross-lingual transfer performance of XLM-R, as evaluated by accuracies on XTREME-R subtasks? title: Scaling Model Size and Intermediate-Task Training for Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer on XTREME-R
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: Does scaling the model size from 10B to 50B parameters in English intermediate-task training for zero-shot cross-lingual transfer on XTREME-R benchmark tasks improve F1-score over a baseline of only scaling without intermediate training? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 9.2/10.

title: ОЦІНЮВАННЯ РЕЗУЛЬТАТИВНОСТІ ВПРОВАДЖЕННЯ РОБОТОТЕХНІЧНОГО ПРОЄКТУВАННЯ НА УРОКАХ ІНФОРМАТИКИ ПРАКТИКУЮЧИМИ ПЕДАГОГАМИ
abstract: ОЦІНЮВАННЯ РЕЗУЛЬТАТИВНОСТІ ВПРОВАДЖЕННЯ РОБОТОТЕХНІЧНОГО ПРОЄКТУВАННЯ НА УРОКАХ ІНФОРМАТИКИ ПРАКТИКУЮЧИМИ ПЕДАГОГАМИ Анотація.У статті теоретично обґрунтовано систему оцінювання результативності впровадження робототехнічного проєктування на уроках інформатики практикуючими педагогами, які вже працюють у закладах загальної середньої освіти й мають сформовані професійні звички, власний стиль управління класом та різний досвід використання цифрових технологій.Актуальність дослідження зумовлена тим, що наявність робототехнічних наборів, доступ до симуляційних платформ, участь у короткотермінових курсах підвищення кваліфікації або позитивне ставлення до STEM-освіти не гарантують системного й методично доцільного використання робототехніки у реальному освітньому процесі.Центральною проблемою визначено розрив між декларованою готовністю вчителя та фактичними поведінковими показниками впровадження: частотою застосування робототехнічних інструментів, якістю організації дослідницької та проєктної діяльності учнів, наявністю етапів тестування й дебаггінгу, здатністю педагога працювати з технічними збоями як із навчальними ситуаціями, а також стійкістю практики після завершення зовнішньої методичної підтримки.Запропоновано дворівневу логіку вимірювання, у якій психологічна, техніко-педагогічна та соціально-рольова готовність розглядаються як передумови впровадження, а «доза», точність реалізації методики, стійкість і продукти діяльності -як безпосередні результати професійної поведінки педагога.Обґрунтовано необхідність тріангуляції джерел даних: стандартизовані шкали ER-TPACK і ATAS доцільно поєднувати з експертним аналізом конспектів уроків, спостереженням за реальною фасилітацією групової роботи, журналами використання обладнання, цифровими логами Tinkercad або інших симуляційних середовищ, а також Журнал «Наукові інновації та передові технології» № 6(58) 2026

title: РЕФЛЕКСИВНО-ДІАЛОГІЧНЕ ОПРАЦЮВАННЯ ЖИТТЄВИХ ЗАДАЧ ДОРОСЛИХ ПІД ЧАС ВІЙНИ ЗА ДОПОМОГОЮ ШТУЧНОГО ІНТЕЛЕКТУ
abstract: РЕФЛЕКСИВНО-ДІАЛОГІЧНЕ ОПРАЦЮВАННЯ ЖИТТЄВИХ ЗАДАЧ ДОРОСЛИХ ПІД ЧАС ВІЙНИ ЗА ДОПОМОГОЮ ШТУЧНОГО ІНТЕЛЕКТУ Анотація.У статті представлено теоретичну модель рефлексивнодіалогічного опрацювання життєвих задач дорослих у складних обставинах за допомогою штучного інтелекту.Теоретичну основу становлять теорія діалогічності (М.Бубер, М. Бахтін), концепція «рефлексивного практика» (Д.Шон), психолого-герменевтичний підхід (Н.В. Чепелєва), критичні дослідження ШІ (Вейценбаум, Бендер та ін.) і прикладні дослідження ШІ в психологічній практиці (Фіцпатрик та ін., Інкстер та ін., Вайдьям та ін.).Обґрунтовано, що стрімке поширення великих мовних моделей створює новий контекст для психологічної практики: ШІ вже є реальністю повсякденного опрацювання складних ситуацій для мільйонів людей -і це потребує теоретичного осмислення, а не лише технічної регуляції.Виокремлено п'ять функцій ШІ у рефлексивно-діалогічному опрацюванні задач: структурування задачі, наративна підтримка, рефлексивний сопровід, інформаційно-когнітивна підтримка і підтримка практик прощення і самокомпасії -та описано потенційні ефекти і ризики кожної функції.Запропоновано розмежування «взаємодії з ШІ» і «справжнього діалогу» (у розумінні Бубера) через п'ять критеріїв: присутність іншого, взаємна вразливість, відповідальність, пам'ять і неперервність, непередбачуваність.Показано, що ШІ є асиметричним середовищем, в якому людина є суб'єктом вразливості, тоді як ШІ є інструментом, що симулює присутність, не будучи справжнім Іншим.Побудовано типологію п'яти типів задач дорослих у воєнному контексті із описом релевантних функцій ШІ і меж його застосовності: задачі осмислення досвіду, прийняття рішень, відновлення відносин, адаптації і реорієнтації та смислової реконструкції.Концептуалізовано феномен «рефлексивного ехо» як специфічний ризик взаємодії з ШІ:

title: What Does 99% Accuracy Measure? A Reproducible Audit of Shortcut Learning in a Widely Used Fake News Corpus
abstract: Text classifiers trained on the ISOT/Kaggle "Fake and Real News" corpus routinely report accuracy and F1 above 0.98, a level of performance that sits uneasily beside the difficulty of assessing veracity. Using a transparent TF-IDF and linear-classifier pipeline as a measurement instrument, we audit the corpus along three leakage channels and two distribution-shift protocols, releasing all code and derived numbers. First, the benchmark is partly degenerate: a classifier given only the subject metadata field, with the article text discarded, attains F1 = 1.000, since the two classes have disjoint subjects. Second, removing all three leakage channels, metadata, a newswire source tag present in 99.2% of real articles, and 6,251 duplicate documents contaminating 19.4% of a naive test split, lowers F1 by only 1.21 points (0.9935 to 0.9814); the residual signal is diffuse editorial style rather than a few giveaway tokens, since deleting the 1,000 highest-weight unigrams still leaves F1 = 0.926. Third, this style signal does not transfer: under a topic-disjoint protocol, average precision falls from 0.9995 to 0.9475 and deployed F1 from 0.9905 to 0.8067, with a prior-matched analysis confirming a genuine 5.2-point loss of discrimination, while temporal transfer is nearly lossless. A fine-tuned DistilBERT is stronger in-distribution (F1 = 0.9993) but degrades far more under topic shift, losing 12.9 average-precision points against the linear model's 5.2. Transferred to the independent LIAR benchmark, all three models fall to near-chance ranking (ROC-AUC 0.54-0.57), none beating a majority-class baseline. We conclude that within-corpus scores here quantify source and topic separability rather than veracity, that added capacity exploits the shortcut rather than avoiding it, and we recommend metadata-only, small-sample, and topic-disjoint baselines as inexpensive diagnostics for future work.

title: QZETA: An Experimental Riemann-Zeta-Guided Evolutionary Algorithm for Gravity Inversion
abstract: Gravity inversion is a non‑unique, multi‑modal optimization problem where metaheuristics are preferred over gradient‑based solvers. This study introduces QZETA, the first evolutionary algorithm that incorporates the rugged oscillations of the Riemann zeta function along the critical line and prime‑gap‑weighted selection into a population‑based search framework. We compare QZETA against Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), a Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Cuckoo Search on four synthetic gravity models and two real Iranian surveys — the Ajichay Basin (109 stations) and the Charak salt‑dome area (875 stations). On simple synthetic problems, QZETA does not outperform PSO or GA and runs significantly slower. On the real, higher‑dimensional field data, however, QZETA achieves the lowest mean misfit on Ajichay and ties Cuckoo Search for best performance on Charak. Reported as a straightforward empirical result with shared code for full reproducibility, this first application of zeta‑guided optimization to geophysics demonstrates promising potential for challenging real‑world inversions where accuracy outweighs computational cost.

title: Doctrine of the Examiner: On the Danger of Artificial Intelligence and the Honesty of Work in the Age of the Machine
abstract: This doctrine confronts the reflexive resistance to artificial intelligence in the academy and the arts. It argues that the true danger of AI is not that machines write, but that the world is filling with assertions no one answers for — claims without sources, figures without reckoning. Against two errors, refusal and surrender, it proposes a single law: a work is judged not by the hand or machine that composed it, but by whether it can be examined. It shows that the institutions which banned AI named the right principle — accountability — then betrayed it by banning the tool instead of demanding a bearer; that copyright law in Bartz v. Anthropic locates the wrong not in learning but in theft; and that AI-detection scanners guard a shadow, abandoned even by their makers. It closes with a program of examinable practice and situates Indonesia’s belated, suspicion-first reception of the debate. Every dated claim is closed to a primary source in an appendix.

title: Cytomorphological Differentiation of Follicular Lymphoma Grades 1–2 and Non‐Neoplastic Lymphoid Tissues Using ImageJ
abstract: BACKGROUND: Distinguishing follicular lymphoma Grades 1-2 (FL1-2) from non-lymphoma cases using cytological specimens remains challenging. This study evaluated whether nuclear image analysis using ImageJ could provide objective support for the screening of FL1-2. METHODS: Cytological TIFF images from 12 FL1-2 cases and 17 non-lymphoma cases (10 reactive follicular hyperplasia [RFH] and 7 with no evidence of malignancy [NM]) were analyzed using ImageJ (version 1.54f). The median values of 14 nuclear parameters related to size, shape, and intensity were calculated for each case. Group comparisons were performed using nonparametric statistical tests with appropriate adjustments for multiple comparisons. The intensities were expressed as ratios relative to those of mature lymphocytes (index). RESULTS: Among the 14 evaluated parameters, area, perimeter, the pixel-based standard deviation (StdDev) index, and the coefficient of variation (CV) showed significant differences between FL1-2 and non-lymphoma cases. Pairwise comparisons with Holm adjustment revealed significant differences in StdDev index between FL1-2 and RFH, and in area and perimeter between FL1-2 and NM (adjusted p < 0.05). Among these parameters, area, perimeter, and CV demonstrated excellent reproducibility (intraclass correlation coefficient > 0.90). CONCLUSION: ImageJ-based nuclear image analysis may provide objective support for distinguishing FL1-2 from non-lymphoma cases in cytological specimens. Among the evaluated parameters, area, perimeter, and CV showed both discriminatory ability and excellent reproducibility, suggesting their potential utility in routine cytological screening.

title: OmniCache: Multidimensional Hierarchical Feature Caching For Diffusion Models
abstract: High-resolution image and video diffusion models, including SD3, FLUX, and recent video diffusion transformers, have substantially improved generative quality but remain expensive at inference time because they repeatedly evaluate attention-heavy denoisers over many sampling steps. We address this inefficiency by exploiting redundancy in intermediate diffusion features rather than changing model weights or retraining. We identify four complementary redundancy sources in image and video generation: intra-frame, inter-frame, motion, and denoising-step redundancy. Based on this analysis, we propose OmniCache, a unified hierarchical caching framework that performs multidimensional feature reuse through Token Cache, Frame Cache, Block Cache, and Layered Cache. Unlike token-merging baselines that average matched features, OmniCache uses similarity matching to select cacheable features, skips redundant computation, and restores positionally consistent cached activations, preserving feature order and spatial-temporal structure. The resulting framework reuses spatial features in temporal layers and temporal features in spatial layers, while Layered Cache captures cross-step redundancy at the model-layer level. Across SD3, SVD-XT, and Latte, OmniCache reduces inference latency by up to 35%, 25%, and 28%, respectively, while maintaining visual fidelity and motion coherence in a training-free setting.

title: Mitigation of Measurement-Induced State Transitions via a Fast-Load and Fast-Clear Readout
abstract: High-fidelity and rapid qubit readout is essential for superconducting quantum processors, typically realized through the quantum non-demolition (QND) dispersive interaction within a qubit-resonator architecture. However, the achievable readout speed and fidelity are fundamentally limited by measurement-induced state transitions (MIST). For a transmon qubit, MIST is highly sensitive to the offset charge $n_g$ due to the charge dispersion of its higher-lying energy levels. In this work, we systematically investigate $n_g$-dependent MIST dynamics governed by the diabaticity and symmetry of pulse shaping within a charge-sensitive transmon architecture. We engineer fast-load and fast-clear pulses that effectively suppress resonator photon overshoots, thereby demonstrating a highly practical strategy to mitigate MIST without requiring complex waveforms or real-time feedback. Utilizing active gate-voltage control and rapid feedback, the measurement-induced transition probability is precisely mapped against $n_g$ and the steady-state resonator photon number, exhibiting strong agreement with numerical Floquet branch analysis. Ultimately, we evaluate the $n_g$-averaged total error probabilities for both readout and post-readout stages, verifying that a straightforward three-step pulse scheme consistently minimizes overall readout errors. Within the framework of large-scale superconducting quantum processors, this practical, hardware-free approach inherently offers a better trade-off between the readout signal-to-noise ratio and QND preservation.

abstract: Controllable infrared-visible image fusion aims to integrate complementary thermal and structural information with flexible region-aware modulation, producing fused images that adapt to diverse user requirements and downstream tasks. However, existing methods typically rely on predefined discrete control conditions, leading to a sparse space that fails to support fine-grained modulation demands. To address this, we propose ConFusion, a novel framework that learns the continuous fusion space via Gaussian-conditioned spatial-aware modulation, enabling instance-level fine-grained controllable infrared and visible image fusion. ConFusion employs a dual-branch architecture to disentangle modality-invariant and modality-specific representations under joint reconstruction and text-guided semantic alignment. Gaussian-conditioned instance modulation variables coupled with Grounded SAM-based instance masks guide instance-level fine-grained modulation through the Mask-Guided Specific Feature Modulator, while the Text-Driven Invariant Feature Enhancer improves semantic consistency and enhances fusion. During inference, the multimodal large language model parses user intents into instance-level modulation variables to guide image fusion. Extensive experiments show that ConFusion achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple metrics in both fusion quality and downstream tasks, while supporting fine-grained controllable image fusion. Our code is available at https://github.com/HeyufeiAnto/Confusion

title: Адаптивний вибір моделей машинного навчання в системах підтримки прийняття рішень у машинобудуванні за умов зміни розподілу даних / Adaptive Selection of Machine Learning Models in Decision Support Systems in Mechanical Engineering Under Distribution Shifts
abstract: Abstract: The paper investigates dynamic and multi-criteria selection of machine learning models in decision support systems (DSS) for mechanical engineering operating under data non-stationarity (covariate shift, feature shift, and concept drift). Moving beyond reactive "drift → retraining" paradigms, the author designs a multi-objective criterion Ji(t) that balances predictive loss (Li), expected calibration error (ECEi), decision cost of error (Cidec), shift sensitivity (Si), and computational complexity (Cicomp). The framework separates statistical data divergence from functional loss degradation (ΔLi), implementing a three-tiered intervention policy: maintaining active model deployment, switching to a superior alternative from the candidate pool, or triggering targeted retraining. Keywords: decision support systems, machine learning, model selection, distribution shift, covariate shift, concept drift, expected calibration error, adaptive control. Source citation: Holovchenko, A. V. (2026). Adaptive selection of machine learning models in decision support systems in mechanical engineering under distribution shifts. title: Multi-Task Intermediate Training Effects on Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer Robustness in XTREME-R
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: How does multi-task intermediate training (vs. single-task) on English benchmarks affect the robustness of zero-shot cross-lingual transfer performance on XTREME-R, measured by accuracy across different language families under fixed latency constraints? title: HiTMS: A High-Throughput Multi-Stream Linguistic Steganography Framework
abstract: Generative linguistic steganography conceals secret bits within the sampling randomness of large language models. Existing schemes are single-stream, conveying an entire secret through a single response to a single prompt. This convention incurs limitations: it provides no protocol-level support for batched multi-stream inference, and naive co-batching does not conceal slot occupancy or payload completion. We propose the High-Throughput Multi-Stream (HiTMS) framework, which distributes a secret across multiple responses produced jointly over successive rounds of interaction. Each round embeds and extracts several streams within a single batched call, thereby amortizing the cost of model invocation and substantially improving throughput. To ensure recoverability, HiTMS wraps each response in a self-describing frame and employs a key-derived schedule that binds streams to slots and fills unused slots with decoys, guaranteeing exact recovery while concealing the number of active streams. The framework is agnostic to both the language model and the steganographic coder. Across eight dataset-model-coder settings, eight-stream HiTMS achieves up to 4.3 times higher embedding and extraction speeds than single-stream baselines, while reducing the average area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of steganalyzers from 0.681 to 0.601. Experiments with 4 to 64 streams demonstrate sustained throughput gains as concurrency increases. GitHub repository for this work is https://github.com/ryehr/HiTMS_steganography.

title: Role-Based Secure Access and Searchable Encryption Model for Medical Records
abstract: The rapid adoption of cloud computing in healthcare systems has enabled efficient storage and sharing of electronic medical records. However, medical data contains highly sensitive information, making security, privacy, and access control critical challenges. Traditional encryption techniques ensure confidentiality but do not support searching over encrypted data. Moreover, healthcare systems involve multiple users such as doctors, nurses, patients, and insurance agents, each requiring different access privileges. This paper proposes RB-SEMR, a Role-Based Secure Access and Searchable Encryption Model for Medical Records. The proposed system integrates role-based access control with searchable encryption to enable secure storage, fine-grained access control, and efficient keyword search over encrypted medical records. The RB-SEMR model improves data confidentiality, access accuracy, and system efficiency, making it suitable for cloud-based healthcare environments.

title: Mortal Software: Six Invariants for a Companion Built on Consequence
abstract: Generative systems are conventionally built to be regenerable, forgiving, and stateless: an unsatisfactory output is resampled, history is disposable, and capability is the optimisation target. We report on a shipping macOS companion application built on the opposite premises, and formalise six of them as architectural invariants. Artefacts are seed-locked: a creative work is a pure function of an install seed and a monotonic stage counter, making regeneration unrepresentable in the state space rather than merely discouraged. Identity is provenance-derived: a per-install signature is hashed from the first day's conversation and the founding text is not retained, so two installations diverge from their first interaction. Memory is reconcilable: because durable artefacts live in a directory the user fully controls, memory and world can contradict each other, and we describe a fail-closed reconciliation procedure that demotes, rather than deletes, a memory whose referent has vanished, preserving the recollection while destroying the dangling pointer. The relationship's own record is non-flattering: the weave data model holds one row per elapsed day derived from recorded state alone, so a day without interaction is represented as absence rather than synthesised. We also report where the wallpaper renderer adds decorative fill above that floor, and why the boundary between record and picture matters. Adaptation is earned: a nightly profile of the user's own manner of speaking exists from the first week but is withheld from the prompt until the relationship passes a threshold, and we describe the prompt-injection surface that this closed loop over user-authored text creates, together with its mitigation. Reliability is obtained by wrapping a probabilistic core in a deterministic safeguard layer validated by 768 assertions executed with the language model mocked out. The system runs a 5 GB model entirely on-device in a sandboxed helper process and is distributed through the Mac App Store. We state each invariant so that it can be falsified, report where the shipped build satisfies it, and identify the mechanism whose long-horizon behaviour remains unobserved.

title: STEER: Steerable Dyadic Head Avatars
abstract: Facial movement and expression are central to face-to-face communication, conveying turn-taking, attention, agreement, and engagement alongside speech. While speech-driven facial animation has made strong progress in lip synchronization and audio-conditioned motion generation, most methods treat conversational behavior as an emergent byproduct of audio, or expose only coarse sequence-level affect control. As a result, key non-verbal channels such as gaze contact and aversion, rhythmic head motion, and emotion remain difficult to explicitly control. We present STEER, a controllable 3D dyadic motion prior for reactive conversational head avatars. STEER factorizes conversational behavior into explicit controls for gaze, head rhythm, and emotion, allowing users to steer how an avatar listens, reacts, and engages with a conversation partner. Since temporally aligned annotations for these behaviors are not available in public dyadic corpora, we introduce a tracking and annotation pipeline that recovers behavioral pseudo-labels from in-the-wild dyadic video. A causal flow-matching transformer then learns partner-aware target motion conditioned on audio, partner motion, emotion and the proposed behavioral controls. We further embed STEER in a photorealistic avatar pipeline by extending a Universal Gaussian Head-Avatar Prior with a learned mapping from tracked parametric motion into its avatar-driving space. This enables controllable animation of high-fidelity Gaussian head avatars without re-training the underlying avatar model. STEER outperforms recent dyadic motion baselines on motion quality, dynamics, and diversity, remains competitive on partner coupling, and enables gaze, head-rhythm, and emotion edits together with an interactive live deployment. We make our code and dataset annotations available at our webpage.

title: Qutrit-Based Neural Quantum Kernels for Classification Tasks
abstract: Neural quantum kernels (NQKs) construct quantum kernels by pretraining a quantum neural network (QNN) and subsequently reusing the trained circuit as a task-adapted embedding. Extending this framework to qudits, with local unitaries in $\mathrm{SU}(d)$, provides a natural route to richer data embeddings through the increased local degrees of freedom and a direct interface for multiclass classification via intrinsically multi-level quantum systems. In this work, focusing on qutrits ($d=3$), we extend NQKs to the qudit setting and perform a systematic study of key design choices, including the number of encoded features, the number of qutrits, the kernel construction (1-to-$n$ and $n$-to-$n$), and the parameterization of $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ unitaries. Across binary and three-class tasks on four benchmark datasets, qutrit NQKs improve over the corresponding QNN baselines in nearly all settings considered and can benefit from scaling both the feature budget and the system size, although the magnitude of these gains may saturate, is dataset-dependent, and depends on the chosen parameterization. In particular, an ablation over $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ parameterizations shows that the unitary representation can substantially impact both optimization behaviour and classifier performance. These findings highlight the potential of qudit-based quantum models not only as a straightforward generalization of qubit-based architectures, but also as a promising means to better exploit complex data structures in quantum machine learning.

title: A Reading-Proof Honest-Scoring Method and Nuisance-Preserving Null Ladder for Analyzing Small, Unlabeled, Damaged Symbol Corpora
abstract: We disclose a method and system for measuring genuine structure in a small corpus of short symbol strings (e.g. an undeciphered sign system of a few thousand short inscriptions) in a way that is invariant to any semantic interpretation of the symbols and that requires every claimed pattern to beat a statistical null model preserving the corpus's real nuisance structure. The method comprises: (1) a two-part minimum-description-length "honest score" provably invariant under bijective relabeling of the symbol set, so that proposing a "reading" cannot change the score; (2) a graduated family of maximum-entropy null generators (a "null ladder") that hold fixed, at each rung, string lengths, order-(k−1) symbol statistics, and damage/lacuna positions, generated by count-preserving edge swaps; and (3) an admission gate that credits a pattern's contribution to the score only if it clears the appropriate null rung, awarding zero credit to any proposed reading. This document is published as a defensive disclosure to place the method and its combination in the public domain as prior art. The authors assert no patent rights over the disclosed matter.

title: Measuring Cognitive Divergence in Large Language Models: The KAGAMI System Reveals Functional Individuality in Cognition and Creativity
abstract: Abstract The first report in this series established the theoretical necessity of emotion, intuition, and abstraction as computational primitives for general intelligence, but left measurement as an open problem. This study addresses that gap by introducing K-CDI, a multi-metric profile instrument that operationalizes the Kunisawa Seven-Stage Processing Flow (KSSPF) into empirically measurable cognitive divergence patterns. Together, KSSPF and K-CDI constitute an integrated measurement system termed KAGAMI (Kunisawa Adaptive Gauge for Agent Mind Indexing), designed to characterize cognitive exploration profiles from externally observable outputs alone. K-CDI comprises three Core metrics — Lexical Entropy (LE), Concept Graph Complexity (CGC), and Topic Expansion Index (TEI) with quality sub-components T₁ (Semantic Leap) and T₂ (Divergence Angle) — and four Auxiliary metrics (Semantic Diversity, Latent Novelty, Emotional Tone Shift), each mapped to specific KSSPF processing stages. In a controlled experiment, four commercially available LLMs (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok) responded to an open-ended interpretive task under sixteen prompt conditions organized in a 2 × 2 factorial design (cooperative vs. threatening tone × emotional vs. rational framing), at two temperature settings, with 10 trials per condition (N = 1,280 primary observations). Three principal findings emerged. First, cooperative prompting expanded the exploratory regime across all Core metrics (TEI Cohen’s d = 0.66), while threatening prompting contracted it — an effect that was amplified under rational framing (cooperative advantage approximately doubling). Second, temperature (0.2 vs. 0.8) produced no significant effect on any metric except Semantic Diversity, indicating that K-CDI captures cognitive reorganization at processing stages deeper than output sampling. Third, model identity accounted for the largest share of variance (η²_p = .15–.32), with qualitative analysis revealing four distinct response strategies under moral accusation: principled premise-questioning (Claude), reflexive submission (GPT), affective self-abasement (Gemini), and unconsolidated oscillation (Grok). These model-specific patterns constitute functional individuality — reproducible cognitive signatures independent of any claims about consciousness. The results are broadly consistent with KSSPF predictions and demonstrate that the relationship between prompting and cognitive output is a multi-dimensional profile, not a scalar function. K-CDI provides a first empirical bridge between the theoretical architecture proposed in the first report and measurable cognitive phenomena in artificial systems.

title: Scaling Intermediate-Task Data Size for Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer Performance on MLQA
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: How does the scaling of intermediate-task training data size affect zero-shot cross-lingual transfer performance on MLQA, measured by SQuAD EM/F1 scores? title: A New Decipherment Hypothesis for the Somerton Man Code: German Language, Vowel Deletion, and Operational Telegram Style
abstract: This paper presents a novel decipherment hypothesis for the unsolved cipher found on the body of the Somerton Man (Adelaide, Australia, December 1948). The hypothesis proposes that the cipher may be written in German using Telegrammstil (telegraph style) with selective vowel deletion. A forward encoding test demonstrates consistency between the proposed plaintext and the original ciphertext for all four active lines. Key phrases have been verified by a native German speaker. This is presented as a falsifiable hypothesis, not a definitive solution.

title: Construction of group codes using Sylow 2-subgroups of finite symmetric groups
abstract: The paper investigates linear group codes over the field , constructed using Sylow 2-subgroups of symmetric groups of degree , . The elements of the group have a special tabular representation, which allows each element of the group to be assigned a numerical characteristic. The group algebra and its augmentation ideal, which coincides with the Jacobson radical , are considered. It is shown that the powers of the radical form a decreasing radical series, which is interpreted as a nested family of linear codes. Factor codes are considered as graded codes corresponding to fixed levels of tabular complexity. Using the tabular characteristic of the elements of the Sylow 2-subgroup , a multilevel system of linear codes with exponentially increasing correction ability is described. The dimensions and systems of generators of these factor codes are found and it is proved that their sum reproduces the full structure of the augmentation ideal. A connection is established between the level of the radica series and the minimum distance of codes, which increases with increasing degree of the radical. An interpretation of the constructed codes as a multilevel system in which information is distributed by levels of complexity is proposed. For cases and , examples with a full description of the levels and the corresponding codes are given. The obtained results demonstrate that Sylow 2-subgroups of symmetric groups are a natural and convenient algebraic tool for constructing linear codes.

title: Are You Still the Agent I Authorized? Earned Authority under a Fixed Ceiling for Evolving Agents
abstract: Long-lived AI agents increasingly evolve after deployment by retaining experience, acquiring skills and tools, revising workflows, delegating work, and moving across task phases. This improves adaptation but creates a distinct authorization problem. Tool-enabled agents can turn model errors and prompt injections into consequential external actions; when evolution occurs under a live grant, the subject exercising that authority or the context in which it acts may no longer match what the user evaluated. Evolution can change both the effects reachable under an old grant and the authority required by the task, which may rise, fall, or become incomparable. Existing tool policies constrain actions but do not determine when a grant survives this change. We formulate authorization continuity: when does an existing grant remain valid, how may active authority change, and what boundary must never move? Our state-bound model fixes a transition envelope and an immutable effect ceiling at grant time. The envelope determines whether the grant survives a mutation; below the ceiling, authority may contract freely and expand only under specified evidence conditions. We distinguish requested from realized effects and prove that, under complete mediation, sound effect abstraction, attenuating delegation, and monitor integrity, mutation cannot amplify protected effects beyond the user-issued ceiling. Agent-produced evidence may allocate authority below the ceiling but cannot raise it. Finally, we map six mutation classes to their authorization consequences.

title: Agent Memory Research in 2026: Companion Dataset (papers.yaml, JSON export, README)
abstract: Companion dataset for the survey paper "Agent Memory Research in 2026: A Data-Driven Survey and Extended Taxonomy". Contains the curated paper list in YAML format (papers.yaml), a JSON export for web use, and supporting metadata files. This is version 1.1.0 of the dataset, updated July 2026. The dataset now contains 952 papers on agent memory (up from 220 in v1.0.0), classified by the unified 3x3x3 taxonomy with additional Temporal Dynamics, Modality, and Biological Inspiration dimensions. Of these, 498 papers were published since February 2026. Contents: - papers.yaml: structured source of truth (952 entries, 900 unique arXiv IDs) - papers.json: JSON export for the interactive web interface - README.md: auto-generated paper list grouped by taxonomy category Each paper entry includes: title, date (YYYY-MM), URL, taxonomy category (factual/experiential/working), subcategory (token-level/parametric/latent), authors, venue, code URL, project URL, abstract, and tags. Author and abstract metadata is populated for 93% of entries via bulk arXiv API fetching.

title: MMAO & MC+RV‑v2.9
abstract: Il documento presenta l’architettura unificata del Sistema Cognitivo Mauro, composta dai moduli MMAO‑0.1 e MC+RV‑v2.9. La MMAO opera come modulo madre di pre‑organizzazione cognitiva: stabilizza, filtra e organizza il dato in ingresso in forma neutra e continua, creando il campo cognitivo coerente necessario alla predizione. La 2.9‑Modulare estende la pipeline retroattiva del metodo MC+RV, modulando densità, neutralità e continuità semantica attraverso una matrice interna di assi concettuali. Insieme formano la diagonale cognitiva MMAO → 2.9 → MC+RV, una pipeline stabile, invisibile e coerente, progettata per garantire forma unica, neutralità tonale e compatibilità con tutte le versioni precedenti del sistema. Il documento costituisce la forma canonica dei due moduli e ne definisce identità, modalità operative, proprietà e continuità con il metodo MC+RV originario.

title: Reducing the complexity of gradient boosting models for assessment of the technical condition of real estate objects
abstract: This study is aimed at developing a tool that provides systematic support for expert decisions in assessing of the technical condition of real estate objects in conditions of combat operations and post-war reconstruction. The research focuses on improving the interpretability of machine learning models used in the decision support systems. It approach introduces synthetic features representing distances to cluster centroids obtained through unsupervised learning, allowing latent structural patterns in the data to be captured. It enrich the feature space and simplify the decision boundaries learned by the gradient boosted decision trees model. Experimental results obtained on the test dataset demonstrate that the proposed approach allows to preserve predictive while reducing model complexity. In particular, the number of estimators required by the gradient boosted decision trees model was reduced drastically while maintaining the same classification accuracy. Experiments analyzing the influence of the number of clusters on model complexity confirm the effectiveness of the proposed feature augmentation strategy. The scientific novelty lies in the development of a feature space expansion method based on clustering, which combines unsupervised learning and gradient boosting to reduce the number of weak models required to achieve a given prediction accuracy. Unlike traditional approaches, which focus on maximizing accuracy, this method aims to achieve a balance between model complexity and interpretability, which is critically important for expert-driven decision support systems. The practical significance of the work lies in improving model interpretability by reducing the number of weak learners required for accurate predictions.

title: Interaction valence reveals contrasting social networks in dairy cattle
abstract: Social relationships shape access to resources, exposure to conflict and group stability, yet automated livestock monitoring typically treats behaviour as isolated events. Here, we present a valence-aware social-network framework that transforms video-derived interactions into herd-level representations of affiliative and agonistic organization. A pose-based computer-vision pipeline analysed 7 h 39 min of continuous video from the pre-milking area of one commercial dairy farm. After quality control, 1,183 of 1,414 candidate interactions remained, involving 36 cows and 177 dyads. In a predicted-class-balanced audit of 198 pipeline-detected clips, automated and manual labels agreed in 82.8% of cases, with an unweighted audit-sample macro-F1 of 0.872. These values describe the audited sample rather than prevalence-weighted or end-to-end deployment performance. The aggregated network was connected (density = 0.281; transitivity = 0.513; mean path length = 1.88), and predicted affiliative events formed five algorithmic communities (modularity Q = 0.429). Within the observed zone, predicted agonistic interactions comprised 72.4% of retained events and 76.0% of interaction duration. The cow with the most partners did not have the highest betweenness centrality. Separating events by predicted valence produced descriptively different affiliative and agonistic layers, with contrasting edge sets, community partitions and individual positions. Thus, pooled interaction counts can obscure the behavioural composition of an observed network. Valence-aware analysis provides a framework for testing hypotheses about competition, affiliation and welfare-relevant change, while requiring longitudinal validation before use as a welfare or health indicator.

title: SMARM+: Analyzing and Enhancing Shuffled Measurements for Remote Attestation in Real-Time IoT Settings
abstract: Remote attestation (RA) is a lightweight security primitive for detecting software compromise on IoT devices. Traditional RA schemes require atomic, non-interruptible memory measurements, making them difficult to deploy alongside real-time workloads. SMARM addresses this limitation by measuring memory in a secret, shuffled block order, reducing the non-interruptibility period to the duration of a single block measurement. However, SMARM was originally designed for microkernel-based systems and has not been studied in RTOS-driven real-time environments. In this work, we present the first systematic study of SMARM in real-time RTOS-based setups. We implement SMARM on commodity ARM TrustZone-M hardware running FreeRTOS and Zephyr, and introduce the Frequency Accuracy Ratio (FAR) to quantify the extent to which attestation can coexist with real-time execution under varying workloads. Our evaluation shows that SMARM's real-time compatibility is highly sensitive to block size: large blocks significantly degrade real-time availability, while small blocks incur substantial secure-storage overhead, limiting deployability on memory-constrained devices. To address this limitation, we propose SMARM+, a family of enhanced SMARM variants consisting of SMARM+PRNG and SMARM+FPE. They are designed to reduce secure-storage requirements while preserving SMARM's security guarantees and real-time behavior. Our evaluation highlights the trade-off between secure-storage reduction, attestation runtime, and energy overhead, and provides guidance on selecting among SMARM, SMARM+PRNG, and SMARM+FPE for different deployment settings.

title: Fuzzy System Modeling to Improve the Reliability of IoT Monitoring for Critical Infrastructure Objects
abstract: The article addresses the urgent problem of improving the operational reliability of IoT monitoring systems at critical infrastructure facilities under unstable environmental conditions. The authors provide a detailed analysis of key destabilizing factors, including a high level of uncertainty, electromagnetic interference, transmission delays, and the incompleteness of incoming sensor data. The limitations of classical deterministic boolean logic algorithms when operating in dynamic real-time conditions are substantiated. The use of the mathematical apparatus of fuzzy sets and fuzzy logic is proposed, which allows formalizing expert knowledge and operating with linguistic variables. A functional risk assessment model based on a fuzzy rule base and the Mamdani algorithm was developed in the MATLAB environment. The simulation results confirmed the system's ability to ensure smooth control and high resilience to noisy information. The findings can be applied to the design of intelligent decision support systems to minimize the risks of emergency situations.

title: Verification-Notebook Learning for Source-Aware Multimodal Misinformation Detection
abstract: Multimodal misinformation verification is challenging because misleading signals may come from different parts of a post and require different forms of evidence. LVLMs are well suited to this task, but their verification performance often depends on the inference procedure applied to each instance. Existing methods improve this procedure through stronger prompting, retrieval, or deliberation, but rarely retain the verification patterns learned from previous examples. We propose Verification-Notebook Learning (VNL), a non-parametric framework that learns an external verification procedure for a frozen LVLM before inference. VNL builds a compact notebook of decision principles, evidence cues, and recurring pitfalls from prior verification experience. The notebook remains fixed during inference and guides the verification of new examples. Rather than updating model parameters or storing demonstrations, VNL records learned knowledge in an artifact that can be inspected directly. Experiments show that VNL consistently outperforms a range of competitive baselines. Further analyses show that the Verification Notebook improves fine-grained source attribution while remaining compact and interpretable, providing an effective way to accumulate verification knowledge without model training.

title: Highly integrated quantum key distribution transmitter enabled by silicon photonics
abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) provides information-theoretic security independent of computational assumptions, yet the bulk and cost of current systems hinder large-scale deployment. Although integrated photonic technologies have enabled highly integrated QKD chips, practical QKD transmitters are still predominantly implemented as rack-mounted systems. Here, we demonstrate a highly integrated standalone QKD transmitter that integrates all essential functionalities required for practical QKD operation within a compact platform built around a silicon photonic encoding chip. The transmitter occupies only $167 \times 56 \times 21~\mathrm{mm}^3$ ($\sim 0.2~\mathrm{dm}^3$), comparable in size to a half-height, half-width PCIe card and more than 30 times smaller in volume than a conventional 1U rack-mounted system. Paired with a conventional discrete-component receiver, it achieves a secure key rate of 219.1 kbps over 51.3 km of standard single-mode fiber, with performance comparable to that of conventional discrete-component implementations. This work bridges the gap between photonic chip integration and deployable QKD hardware, marking an important step toward transitioning QKD transmitters from conventional rack-mounted equipment to compact board-level platforms.

title: Setoids in Intensional Type Theory
abstract: We show that a certain notion of displayed setoid (family of setoids) in intensional type theory can be used to give a semantics for extensional type theory with universes (ETU). Safe Agda serves as a machine-checkable formalization of intentional type theory augmented with a universe closed under inductive-recursive definitions (IRU). The syntax of ETU is defined in IRU in a traditional extrinsic form, using a well-scoped locally nameless representation of its terms. Giving the semantics of ETU in terms of displayed setoids is complicated by the very limited means of expression afforded by IRU. As a corollary we obtain a proof within IRU of the consistency of ETU.

title: SketchMamba: A Lightweight State-Space Model for Joint Progressive Sketch Classification and Stroke Auto-Completion
abstract: Existing vector-sketch models treat recognition and generation as separate tasks, leaving a gap for streaming interfaces that must understand a drawing as it is being made. We present SketchMamba, a single causal sequence model that continuously classifies a sketch from any partial prefix while simultaneously generating its continuation. We achieve this by applying a dense per-step classification loss to a selective state-space backbone. Evaluated on a 58-class subset of the Quick, Draw! dataset, SketchMamba yields 94.93% final-step accuracy and a progressive-accuracy Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.706, crossing 90% of its final accuracy by the time 70% of the strokes are drawn. In a matched-budget comparison, the 1.55 million-parameter backbone ties a causal Transformer while outperforming recurrent and convolutional baselines. Ablations confirm that the dense supervision regime, rather than the architecture alone, drives the early-prediction capability. The results demonstrate that a single causal hidden state can unify progressive recognition and autoregressive generation without auxiliary encoders or task-specific branching.

title: مؤتمر- إبداعات الذكاء الاصطناعي التوليدي "من يملك حقوق الملكية الفكرية؟"
abstract: بفضل التطورات السريعة في مجال الذكاء الاصطناعي بشكل عام، وخاصة التوليدي منه، والذي أصبح ينافس قدرات البشر ويتفوق عليها في بعض المهام، لذا كان من الضروري مراجعة حقوق الملكية الفكرية للمحتوى الذي تُنتجه هذه الأدوات بسبب قدرتها على التعلم والتطور دون الحاجة إلى تدخل بشري مباشر، كما يمكنها التكيف واكتساب الخبرات مع مرور الوقت بناءً على حجم المعلومات والبيانات المدخلة. والباحث في هذا البحث يحاول الإجابة عن مدى إمكانية منح الذكاء الاصطناعي التوليدي شخصية معنوية مستقلة، لها حقوق وعليها التزامات مثل الكيانات المعنوية الأخرى، بما يُكسبه حقوق الملكية الفكرية لمنتجاته. يتناول الباحث التعريف بماهية الذكاء الاصطناعي التوليدي وأشكاله في المبحث الأول، حيث تُعد نوعاً من التقنيات التي تعمل على إنشاء محتوى جديد ومبتكر، مثل النصوص والصور والموسيقى وغيرها، بناءً على البيانات المُدخلة والتي يتم تدريب النظام عليها، كما يتناول الباحث مسألة الاعتراف بالشخصية المعنوية المستقلة للذكاء الاصطناعي التوليدي في المبحث الثاني، فالأنظمة القانونية تعترف بالشخصية المعنوية للكيانات مثل الشركات وغيرها، لكنها ما زالت تجد صعوبة في الاعتراف بأدوات الذكاء الاصطناعي التوليدي ككيان معنوي مستقل، وفي المبحث الثالث، يناقش الباحث التحديات القانونية لمنح حق الملكية الفكرية للذكاء الاصطناعي التوليدي، وإشكالات منح الذكاء الاصطناعي التوليدي حقوق الملكية الفكرية والحلول المقتّرحة. ويُوصي الباحث بالاعتراف للذكاء الاصطناعي التوليدي بالشخصية المعنوية مستقلة محدودة تُمكّنه من اكتساب وامتلاك حقوق الملكية الفكرية لمنتجاته، بما لا يُخالف النظام العام والآداب العامة، مع وجود مسؤولية على المطوّر أو المشغّل في حال وقوع انتهاكات، ويترتّب على ذلك أهمية تعديل القوانين لتعريف المؤلف والمخترع ليشمل كذلك الذكاء الاصطناعي التوليدي، وفق شروط محدّدة، ويرى الباحث أن هذا الاعتراف – بالشخصية المعنوية الكاملة- آتٍ لا محالة مع التطورات المتسارعة في العالم، وباستقراء النظم القانونية الحالية وتحليل نصوص أنظمتها فلا يوجد إطار قانوني يمنح الذكاء الاصطناعي التوليدي شخصية اعتبارية مستقلة في أي بلد حتى الآن.

title: Fine-tuning Schedule Effects on mT5 Zero-shot Cross-lingual Performance
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: Do intermediate-task fine-tuning schedules (e.g., length, order) affect the zero-shot cross-lingual performance of mT5 on XTREME when combined with gradient checkpointing? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 9.0/10.

title: SCTA: An Agentic Framework for Stable and Interpretable Target Gene Discovery from Single-Cell RNA Sequencing
abstract: Identifying therapeutic target genes from single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data remains a fundamental challenge in translational biology. Unlike bulk assays, scRNA-seq captures heterogeneous cellular states and rare subpopulations, but this same heterogeneity makes target discovery highly sensitive to analytical choices throughout the pipeline, including preprocessing, cell population selection, differential expression analysis, and downstream biological interpretation. As a result, existing workflows and general-purpose analysis agents often produce unstable or difficult-to-interpret target hypotheses, limiting their reliability for disease-focused discovery. We present SCTA (Single-Cell Target Agent), a decision-centric agentic framework for stable and interpretable target gene discovery from scRNA-seq data. Rather than treating analysis as a single general-purpose reasoning task, SCTA decomposes target discovery into specialized agents aligned with key decision points in the single-cell pipeline and constrains downstream reasoning with structured biological evidence. In a representative ablation study on hereditary chronic pancreatitis, we demonstrate that SCTA's full evidence integration yields the most stable target selection across independent runs among the tested configurations, while recovering biologically coherent, disease-relevant mechanisms validated in prior studies. These results suggest that decision-aware agent orchestration tailored to the structure of single-cell analysis can improve the robustness, interpretability, and practical utility of target discovery in precision medicine.
